record.paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
record.original_question: Let (B, B) be a maximal Banach ideal, and let X0 and Y0 be Banach spaces such that X0' and Y0 are of cotype 2 and B*(X0, Y0) is not contained in L2(X0, Y0). If B ◦ L∞ has property (I), does it already follow that the B-LRP is not satisfied, even without assuming that B ◦ L∞ is right-accessible? In other words, can the right-accessibility hypothesis on B ◦ L∞ be removed from this implication?

evidence.quote: Corollary 2.6 Let (B, B) be a maximal Banach ideal. Let X0 and Y0 be Banach spaces such that X′0 and Y0 are of cotype 2 and B∗(X0, Y0) 6⊆ L2(X0, Y0). If B ◦ L∞ is right-accessible and has property (I), then the B-LRP is not satisfied.
Problem 2.9 Can we drop the assumption “ B ◦ L∞ is right-accessible” in Corollary 2.6?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $\mathfrak{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A Banach operator ideal $(\mathfrak{B},\mathbf{B})$ is a subclass $\mathfrak{B}\subseteq\mathfrak{L}$ together with an ideal norm $\mathbf{B}$ such that each component $\mathfrak{B}(X,Y)$ is a Banach space, $\mathfrak{B}$ contains all finite-rank operators (with $\mathbf{B}(x'\otimes y)=\|x'\|\|y\|$), and $\mathfrak{B}$ is two-sided ideal-stable under composition with bounded operators. The adjoint ideal $\mathfrak{B}^{\ast}$ is the maximal hull of the dual procedure and $\mathfrak{B}$ is called maximal if $\mathfrak{B}=\mathfrak{B}^{\ast\ast}$ isometrically. The ideal $\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ denotes the maximal Banach ideal of $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-factorable operators, and $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ is the product ideal. The ideal $\mathfrak{L}_2$ consists of operators factoring through a Hilbert space.

A Banach space $Z$ is said to be of cotype 2 if there exists $C>0$ such that for every finite sequence $(z_i)\subseteq Z$,
$$\Big(\sum_i\|z_i\|^2\Big)^{1/2}\le C\Big(\int_0^1\Big\|\sum_i r_i(t)z_i\Big\|^2dt\Big)^{1/2},$$
where $(r_i)$ are the Rademacher functions.

A Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},\mathbf{A})$ is right-accessible if for every finite-rank operator $T\in\mathfrak{A}$ between Banach spaces $X,Y$, every finite-dimensional subspace $E\subseteq X$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a Banach space $Z$, an operator $L\in\mathfrak{L}(X,Z)$ with $\|L|_E\|\le 1$ and $S\in\mathfrak{A}(Z,Y)$ such that $T|_E=SL|_E$ and $\mathbf{A}(S)\le(1+\varepsilon)\mathbf{A}(T)$. The ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is said to have property (I) if a certain (fixed) injectivity-type stability condition for trace dualities holds; specifically, the canonical map between trace functionals on finite rank operators extends consistently to $\mathfrak{A}$-valued operators on $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-spaces.

Finally, given a maximal Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{B},\mathbf{B})$ and Banach spaces $X_0,Y_0$, the $\mathfrak{B}$-Local Reciprocity Property (the $\mathfrak{B}$-LRP) at $(X_0,Y_0)$ is the assertion that the natural local trace duality between $\mathfrak{B}^{\ast}(X_0,Y_0)$ and the finite-rank component holds in a specified isometric way (so that, in particular, $\mathfrak{B}^{\ast}(X_0,Y_0)$ is properly identified through $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty$).

Question. Let $(\mathfrak{B},\mathbf{B})$ be a maximal Banach operator ideal, and let $X_0,Y_0$ be Banach spaces such that the dual $X_0'$ and $Y_0$ are both of cotype 2 and
$$\mathfrak{B}^{\ast}(X_0,Y_0)\not\subseteq\mathfrak{L}_2(X_0,Y_0).$$
Suppose that $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ has property (I). Does it follow that the $\mathfrak{B}$-LRP fails at $(X_0,Y_0)$, without any additional assumption that $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ is right-accessible? Equivalently, can the right-accessibility hypothesis on $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ be removed from this implication?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work resolving this specific question about removing the right-accessibility hypothesis in the implication "property (I) of $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ forces failure of the $\mathfrak{B}$-LRP." No subsequent paper announcing a proof or counterexample was located, so the status appears to be unknown/likely still open.
